gloss: to become free; to have a moment to spare

definitions.gloss: to become free; to finish what one was doing and be available
definitions.explanation: For one's hands to come free — that is, to finish the task at hand and have time for something else. Literally 'one's hands become empty.' Used constantly at work to offer or ask for help.

examples.japanese: {手|て}が{空|あ}いたら{手伝|てつだ}ってください。
examples.english: Please help me when you're free.

examples.japanese: {今|いま}は{手|て}が{空|あ}いていないので、{後|あと}にしてもらえますか。
examples.english: I'm tied up right now — could it wait?

examples.japanese: {手|て}が{空|あ}いている{人|ひと}から{順番|じゅんばん}に{片付|かたづ}けを{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: Whoever was free started clearing up, one after another.

examples.japanese: {午後|ごご}になれば{手|て}が{空|あ}くと{思|おも}うので、そのときに{資料|しりょう}を{見|み}ておきます。
examples.english: I should be free in the afternoon, so I'll look over the materials then.

notes:
STRUCTURE: {手|て} (hand) + が + {空|あ}く (to become empty, to open up).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {手|て}が{空|あ}いたら: when you get a moment
- {手|て}が{空|あ}いている: to be free right now
- {手|て}が{空|あ}いていない: to be busy (the standard polite refusal)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {暇|ひま}になる: to become free — about having no work at all; {手|て}が{空|あ}く is about the gap between tasks
- {時間|じかん}が{空|あ}く: to have a slot open up — about the schedule rather than the person
- {手|て}が{離|はな}せない: to be unable to break away — hands literally occupied at this moment

USAGE:
Asking {手|て}が{空|あ}いていますか is gentler than {忙|いそが}しいですか, because it implies you will wait until the person is ready.
